# Area Profiles: Las Vegas New Construction Buyer Guide

**Researcher:** Area Profile Researcher
**Compiled:** 2026-07-25
**Scope:** Clark County, Nevada only. Pahrump, Mesquite, and Boulder City are excluded. See the exclusions log at the bottom.

---

## How to read this file

Every external fact carries a citation in this format: `value [source: URL | verified: 2026-07-25]`.

Anything I could not verify against a live source says **NOT FOUND**. That is deliberate. A blank is safer than a guess.

Three warnings before you use anything here:

1. **Prices move.** Builder "from" prices change weekly and reflect the base plan on the least desirable lot. Every price below is a snapshot taken on 2026-07-25 unless the source states its own date.
2. **HOA dollar amounts are almost never published by the master associations themselves.** I checked. Mountain's Edge, Skye Canyon, and Summerlin do not post their assessment amounts publicly. Most HOA figures floating around the internet come from third-party realtor blogs with no citation. I have marked those NOT FOUND rather than repeat them. The reliable source for a real number is the builder's HOA budget and the Nevada resale package.
3. **SID and LID amounts are parcel specific.** There is no single "Summerlin SID amount" or "Skye Canyon SID amount." The number depends on the exact lot. The lookup procedure is in the shared section below and it works for every area in this file.

## SHARED SECTION: SID and LID, how they actually work

This section applies to all six areas. Do not repeat the mechanics inside each area profile.

### What a SID is

A special assessment is a charge levied against properties inside a Special Improvement District. Typical improvements are "streets, sidewalks, curbs and gutters, streetlights, sewer and water facilities" [source: https://www.clarkcountynv.gov/government/elected_officials/county_treasurer/understanding-sids | verified: 2026-07-25].

A SID lets a city, county, or town let property owners finance the cost of that infrastructure over 10 to 30 years at low interest rates, with each owner assessed their "benefited share of the improvements" [source: https://www.clarkcountynv.gov/government/departments/public_works_department/programs_and_services/special_improvement_districts.php | verified: 2026-07-25].

Costs are apportioned "in proportion to the special benefits derived" and calculated on a "front foot, area, zone or other equitable basis" [source: https://www.clarkcountynv.gov/government/elected_officials/county_treasurer/understanding-sids | verified: 2026-07-25]. That is why two houses on the same street can owe different amounts.

### The five things a buyer needs to know

| Question | Answer | Source |
|---|---|---|
| How often is it billed? | Semi-annually. Bills are mailed about 60 days before the due date. | [source: https://treasurer.co.clark.nv.us/Public_Web/Special_Assessments/Collections.aspx \| verified: 2026-07-25] |
| Is it part of my property tax bill? | No. It is billed separately. It is "a lien on the property until the assessment is paid off." | [source: https://www.clarkcountynv.gov/government/elected_officials/county_treasurer/understanding-sids \| verified: 2026-07-25] |
| Can I pay it off early? | Yes. In unincorporated Clark County the assessment "can be paid in full at anytime with a three percent (3%) prepayment penalty on the unpaid balance." | [source: https://www.clarkcountynv.gov/government/elected_officials/county_treasurer/sid-payment-options \| verified: 2026-07-25] |
| What if I miss a payment? | A 2% penalty per month on the unpaid balance plus accrued interest. Non-payment can trigger foreclosure proceedings. | [source: https://www.clarkcountynv.gov/government/elected_officials/county_treasurer/sid-payment-options \| verified: 2026-07-25] |
| Where do I look up my parcel? | The Assessment Management Group parcel search. Search by parcel number, owner name, or street name. | [source: https://amgnv.com/parcelsearch_non_pop1.asp \| verified: 2026-07-25] |

### The lookup procedure (give this to every reader)

The Assessment Management Group database covers Clark County, City of Las Vegas, City of North Las Vegas, City of Henderson districts, and City of Mesquite, plus several northern Nevada jurisdictions [source: https://amgnv.com/parcelsearch_non_pop1.asp | verified: 2026-07-25].

1. Get the assessor parcel number (APN) from the builder before you sign anything.
2. Run the APN at https://amgnv.com/parcelsearch_non_pop1.asp
3. Ask for the remaining balance, the annual installment, the final payment year, and the prepayment penalty in writing.
4. Clark County directs SID balance and payoff questions to www.amgnv.com [source: https://www.clarkcountynv.gov/government/elected_officials/county_treasurer/sid-payment-options | verified: 2026-07-25].
5. Henderson bills its LIDs through the same administrator, AMG [source: https://www.cityofhenderson.com/government/departments/finance/lid-special-assessment-property-tax/lid-special-assessments | verified: 2026-07-25]. Note: this page returned HTTP 403 to automated retrieval on 2026-07-25. The URL is correct and loads in a normal browser. Detail beyond "AMG bills Henderson LIDs" should be re-confirmed manually.

**Important gap:** an escrow timing rule appears on the AMG page. Properties closing escrow within 15 days before or after the assessment bill mailing date must have assessments paid from escrow [source: https://amgnv.com/parcelsearch_non_pop1.asp | verified: 2026-07-25]. Worth a sentence in the guide.

### Per-home annual dollar amounts

**NOT FOUND from any primary or government source.** I checked the Clark County Treasurer, Clark County Public Works, the City of Henderson finance department, and AMG. None publishes a per-home or per-community average.

Third-party real estate blogs publish figures that disagree with each other by a factor of five or more for the same master plan. I am not reproducing them. If the guide wants a range, it should say plainly that the amount is parcel specific and hand the reader the lookup steps above.

**One dated third-party data point that is safe to cite as historical, not current:** a Summerlin SID FAQ page states that Summerlin assessments are billed semi-annually through the City of Las Vegas or Clark County, are apportioned on a per-acre basis, and carry prepayment penalties that step down "from 3% to 0% over the term of the bonds." The page is stamped "Updated 07.2019" [source: https://summerlinhomes4sale.com/faqs-about-summerlins-special-improvement-districts-sid/ | verified: 2026-07-25]. Treat this as 2019 information, not 2026.

### Schools: the shared verification rule

Do not print a school name for a specific address without checking it. CCSD rezones.

- Official CCSD zoning page: https://www.ccsd.net/zoning [source: https://www.ccsd.net/zoning | verified: 2026-07-25]
- Official interactive zoning search: https://search.ccsd.net/schools/zoning/search/ [source: https://search.ccsd.net/schools/zoning/search/ | verified: 2026-07-25]
- CCSD registration assistance: (702) 799-7678 [source: https://www.ccsd.net/zoning | verified: 2026-07-25]

CCSD's own search tips: if the first search returns nothing, leave the street number blank and enter only the first three letters of the street name, and never enter a direction (N, S, E, W) or a street type (Ave, Dr, St) in the street field [source: https://www.ccsd.net/zoning | verified: 2026-07-25].

**School ratings:** NOT FOUND from a named, dated source I could verify on 2026-07-25. Per the guide's rules, no school in this file is characterized as good or bad, and no rating number is printed.

### Valleywide market context (use once, at the top of the area chapter)

Las Vegas Realtors reported for **June 2026**:

- Median price of an existing single-family home sold through the MLS: **$490,000**, unchanged from the all-time high set in May 2026, and up 1.0% from June 2025.
- Median price of a local condo or townhome: **$292,000**, down 4.3% from June 2025.
- Total existing homes, condos, and townhomes sold in June 2026: **2,823**.
- Single-family homes listed without offers at the end of June 2026: **7,147**, up 2.2% year over year.
- Condos and townhomes listed without offers: **2,690**, up 4.9% year over year.
- Share of homes selling within 60 days: **78.5%**, down from 82.8% a year earlier.
- Cash sales: **23.2%** of all local property sales.

[source: https://nevadabusiness.com/2026/07/lvr-reports-local-home-prices-hovering-at-record-high/ | verified: 2026-07-25]

**Critical caveat that must appear in the guide:** LVR states its statistics come from its MLS, "which does not account for all newly constructed homes sold by local builders or homes for sale by owners" [source: https://nevadabusiness.com/2026/07/lvr-reports-local-home-prices-hovering-at-record-high/ | verified: 2026-07-25]. The $490,000 figure is a resale number. It is a useful benchmark, not a new construction price.

# AREA 1: SUMMERLIN

## Boundaries and character

Summerlin sits on the western edge of the Las Vegas valley, up against Red Rock Canyon. It covers 22,500 acres [source: https://communities.howardhughes.com/regions/nevada/ | verified: 2026-07-25].

Think of it in two halves. The older, finished half sits east of the 215 Beltway and includes Downtown Summerlin, a 400-acre walkable core with more than 800,000 square feet of retail, the Las Vegas Ballpark, and City National Arena, the Vegas Golden Knights practice facility [source: https://communities.howardhughes.com/regions/nevada/ | verified: 2026-07-25].

The newer, still-building half is west and uphill. Summerlin's developer lists the currently selling areas as being south of the 215 Beltway (The Peaks, Summerlin Centre), in the western region (Stonebridge, Reverence, Redpoint Square, Kestrel, Kestrel Commons), and at Grand Park [source: https://summerlin.com/new-homes-ready-for-quick-move-in-throughout-summerlin-4/ | verified: 2026-07-25].

Freeway access: the 215 Beltway runs through Summerlin north to south. Charleston Boulevard and Sahara Avenue are the main east-west surface routes toward the Strip.

Population: 132,000 residents [source: https://communities.howardhughes.com/regions/nevada/ | verified: 2026-07-25].

## Price band

**Summerlin new construction, May 2026:** roughly the **mid $500,000s at the entry end** (Heritage by Lennar, Quail Cove by KB Home, Lark Hill by Taylor Morrison) **to about $2.4 million at the top** (The Pointe at Ascension by Pulte) [source: https://summerlin.com/new-homes-ready-for-quick-move-in-throughout-summerlin-4/ | verified: 2026-07-25].

Toll Brothers' Ascension Crestline Collection starts at $1,854,995 as of 2026-07-25, which sits above Pulte's Ascension entry [source: https://www.tollbrothers.com/luxury-homes-for-sale/Nevada/Las-Vegas | verified: 2026-07-25].

There is no sub-$500,000 new construction in Summerlin in this data set.

## Master plan status

- Inception: 1990 [source: https://communities.howardhughes.com/regions/nevada/ | verified: 2026-07-25]
- Approximately **5,000 gross acres reserved for future growth** out of 22,500 total [source: https://communities.howardhughes.com/regions/nevada/ | verified: 2026-07-25]
- More than 300 parks and more than 200 miles of trails [source: https://summerlin.com/ | verified: 2026-07-25]
- 949,000 square feet of office [source: https://communities.howardhughes.com/regions/nevada/ | verified: 2026-07-25]

**Percent built out:** NOT FOUND from a Howard Hughes source. Third-party sites claim "over 80%." I could not verify that against an investor disclosure or a Howard Hughes page on 2026-07-25.

**What this means for a buyer:** Summerlin's older villages are finished and their amenities are real and open today. The western villages (Kestrel, Kestrel Commons, Stonebridge, Grand Park) are the active frontier. Amenity status in those specific villages: NOT FOUND. A buyer in Kestrel Commons should ask which park, trail, and school in their village is built versus planned, and get the answer in writing.

## HOA reality

Summerlin uses a master association plus neighborhood sub-associations. Exact monthly dollar amounts: **NOT FOUND**. Neither summerlin.com nor communities.howardhughes.com publishes assessment amounts.

Nevada law gives buyers a route to the real number. Under NRS 116.4109 a resale package must include the association's current operating budget, reserve study summary, financial statement, statement of unpaid and special assessments, transfer fees and other current or expected fees, and a statement of the unit's share of common expenses [source: https://law.justia.com/codes/nevada/chapter-116/statute-116-4109/ | verified: 2026-07-25].

**For new construction the guide should say:** ask the builder for the HOA budget and the projected first-year assessment for both the master and the sub-association, in writing, before signing. Do not accept a verbal number.

## SID and LID exposure

Summerlin carries active districts. Confirmed on the Clark County collections schedule:

- SID 128A, The Summerlin Centre, final payment Dec 1, 2030
- SID 159, Summerlin Village 16A, final payment June 1, 2035
- SID 151, Summerlin-Mesa, final payment already made on June 1, 2025

[source: https://treasurer.co.clark.nv.us/Public_Web/Special_Assessments/Collections.aspx | verified: 2026-07-25]

Summerlin spans both unincorporated Clark County and the City of Las Vegas, so a given village may sit in a county district or a city district. Historic guidance says Summerlin SIDs are billed semi-annually "through the City of Las Vegas or Clark County" and apportioned per acre [source: https://summerlinhomes4sale.com/faqs-about-summerlins-special-improvement-districts-sid/ | verified: 2026-07-25, page stamped "Updated 07.2019"].

**Annual dollar amount per home: NOT FOUND.** Run the APN through AMG. See the shared section.

## Schools

Assigned CCSD schools by village: **NOT FOUND**, verified per the shared rule. Internal research reports disagreed with each other about assignments for homes on the same street, so no internal figure was carried forward.

Verify at https://search.ccsd.net/schools/zoning/search/ by exact address.

**Extra caution for Summerlin West:** in Kestrel, Kestrel Commons, Stonebridge, and Grand Park the zoned school may not be built yet. Ask the builder for the current CCSD assignment letter and understand it can change before your kids start.

## Commute

Distances and drive times below come from third-party travel sources and vary with traffic. They are estimates, not measurements.

- To the Strip: about 12 miles, roughly 17 to 25 minutes [source: https://psswestcoast.com/travel/to-city/how-far-is-summerlin-from-las-vegas/ | verified: 2026-07-25]
- To Harry Reid International Airport: about 17 to 19 miles, roughly 22 to 30 minutes, via the 215 south to I-15 [source: https://luxevegaslifestyles.com/how-far-summerlin-harry-reid-international-airport/ | verified: 2026-07-25]
- To downtown Las Vegas: NOT FOUND from a source I could verify
- To the Henderson medical district (Union Village / Henderson Hospital): NOT FOUND

Valleywide context: Las Vegas has one of the shortest average commutes in the country. A Harris Poll survey for Lyft put the local average travel time at 25.6 minutes [source: https://www.reviewjournal.com/news/news-columns/road-warrior/las-vegas-ranks-among-easiest-commutes-in-u-s-survey-finds-3179817/ | verified: 2026-07-25]. Note that this is a survey, not census data.

## The honest tradeoff

Summerlin is genuinely good at delivering a finished lifestyle. The trails, parks, Downtown Summerlin, and the ballpark exist right now, not on a rendering. The resale market for Summerlin homes is deep. If you are relocating from out of state and you want the least amount of guesswork about what your neighborhood will look like in five years, this is the safest bet in the valley.

What Summerlin is not is affordable. There is no entry-level new construction here. The cheapest new homes in the May 2026 lineup sit in the mid $500,000s and they are small, at 1,264 square feet for the Lennar Heritage plan. To get square footage you move up fast, and the top of the market runs past $2 million. Summerlin is also the farthest western part of the valley, so if your job is in Henderson or on the east side, you are driving across the whole city twice a day. And the newest villages, which is where most of the inventory is, are still construction zones with amenities that are promised rather than built.

# AREA 2: SKYE CANYON AND THE NORTHWEST (CENTENNIAL HILLS)

## Boundaries and character

Skye Canyon sits in northwest Las Vegas, "nestled between the bright lights of the Las Vegas Strip and the tall timbers of Mt. Charleston," just off the US 95 freeway at Skye Canyon Park Drive [source: https://skyecanyon.com/ | verified: 2026-07-25].

**On the Centennial Hills question.** Internal research found zero communities labeled Centennial Hills. That was a labeling problem, not an inventory problem. Centennial Hills is the broader City of Las Vegas district in the far northwest. The active new construction inside it clusters in two master plans, Skye Canyon and Providence, plus the Kyle Canyon area [source: https://www.thelasvegasluxuryhomepro.com/centennial-hills-new-construction-homes/ | verified: 2026-07-25].

Providence is a Focus Property Group master plan in ZIPs 89166 and 89149, bounded roughly by Hualapai Way and Grand Teton Drive [source: https://www.nevadarealestategroup.com/blog/providence-northwest-las-vegas-master-plan-guide-2026/ | verified: 2026-07-25]. Providence's total home count is reported inconsistently across sources (5,600 homes on 1,200 acres in one place, about 8,500 homes on 4,200 acres in another) and neither figure could be confirmed against a Focus Property Group source. **Providence total homes and acreage: NOT FOUND.**

**Recommendation for the guide:** treat "Skye Canyon and the northwest" as one area and say plainly that Centennial Hills is the district name, while Skye Canyon and Providence are the master plans inside it. Do not write a separate Centennial Hills section with no inventory in it.

Freeway access: US 95 is the spine. Skye Canyon Park Drive is the main exit. The 215 Beltway is south of the area.

## Who is building there now

Skye Canyon's own site lists three builders: **Century Communities, Toll Brothers, and LGI Homes**, offering entry-level, move-up, and luxury single family homes and townhomes [source: https://skyecanyon.com/ | verified: 2026-07-25].

The site also states plainly: "Skye Canyon does not sell vacant lots, only Single Family Homes and Townhouses" [source: https://skyecanyon.com/ | verified: 2026-07-25].

Toll Brothers at Skye Canyon, single family, from **$665,000** as of 2026-07-25 [source: https://www.tollbrothers.com/luxury-homes-for-sale/Nevada/Las-Vegas | verified: 2026-07-25].

Century Communities lists Las Vegas metro inventory under ZIP codes 89149 and 89166, both of which are northwest Las Vegas [source: https://www.centurycommunities.com/find-your-new-home/nevada/las-vegas-metro/ | verified: 2026-07-25].

**Unresolved from internal research:** Pulte and Lennar were described in internal reports as active at Skye Canyon (Pinewood, Solitude, Belterra) but do not appear on skyecanyon.com's builder list as of 2026-07-25. Either they have closed out or the master plan site is behind. **Status: NOT FOUND. Verify before naming them.**

## Price band

**Skye Canyon: "From the $400s"** per the master plan's own site [source: https://skyecanyon.com/ | verified: 2026-07-25]. Top end at Toll Brothers starts at $665,000 [source: https://www.tollbrothers.com/luxury-homes-for-sale/Nevada/Las-Vegas | verified: 2026-07-25].

**Centennial Hills overall:** there were 189 new homes for sale at a median listing price of **$515,000** [source: https://www.thelasvegasluxuryhomepro.com/centennial-hills-new-construction-homes/ | verified: 2026-07-25]. This is a third-party aggregation, not an MLS or builder figure, and the source does not state its own data date. Label it accordingly or leave it out.

## Master plan status

Skye Canyon's own site does not publish acreage, planned home count, or percent complete. **NOT FOUND.**

Third-party sources describe Skye Canyon as roughly 1,700 acres developed since 2015 by Olympia Companies, with a long-term target near 9,200 homes and roughly 55% to 60% complete in 2026 [source: https://www.nevadarealestategroup.com/blog/skye-canyon-northwest-las-vegas-master-plan-buyers-guide-2026/ | verified: 2026-07-25]. **This is a single uncorroborated third-party estimate. Do not print it as fact.**

**Amenities that are open today**, per the master plan's own site [source: https://skyecanyon.com/ | verified: 2026-07-25]:

- Skye Canyon Park, outdoor space and trails
- Skye Center, the social hub, with Aspire Coffee House
- Skye Fitness, a gym with a junior Olympic pool
- Trails and bike lanes throughout

The site names no "coming soon" amenities. That is a meaningful signal: the core amenity package appears built, not promised.

Providence, by contrast, was built out largely in the mid 2000s through around 2020 [source: https://www.nevadarealestategroup.com/blog/providence-northwest-las-vegas-master-plan-guide-2026/ | verified: 2026-07-25]. New construction in Providence today is infill, not a growing master plan.

## HOA reality

Skye Canyon confirms it has an HOA but does not publish the amount [source: https://skyecanyon.com/ | verified: 2026-07-25].

**Master and sub-association monthly amounts: NOT FOUND.** Internal research recorded a master figure and one sub-association figure, both uncited, and I could not confirm either live.

Structure to expect: a master association covering Skye Center, Skye Fitness, the park, and the trails, plus a neighborhood sub-association in gated or townhome neighborhoods. Get both numbers in writing from the builder.

## SID and LID exposure

Skye Canyon sits inside the City of Las Vegas, so its districts are city districts, not the Clark County districts listed in the shared section.

A City of Las Vegas Special Improvement District No. 610 covering Skye Canyon Phase 3, a 267-acre site, is described as financing local street improvements, storm sewer, sanitary sewer, drainage, and water projects [source: https://www.nevadarealestategroup.com/blog/sid-lid-taxes-las-vegas-new-construction-2026/ | verified: 2026-07-25]. **This is a third-party description. I could not locate the City of Las Vegas ordinance or bond document on 2026-07-25 to confirm the district number.** Treat the number 610 as unconfirmed.

**Annual dollar amount per home: NOT FOUND.** Internal research had figures spanning roughly 35x inside this one master plan, which is exactly why no number appears here.

**This is the single most important thing for a Skye Canyon buyer to check.** The APN lookup at https://amgnv.com/parcelsearch_non_pop1.asp covers City of Las Vegas districts [source: https://amgnv.com/parcelsearch_non_pop1.asp | verified: 2026-07-25].

## Schools

Assigned CCSD schools: **NOT FOUND**, deliberately. Internal reports gave three different answers for neighborhoods on the same street, including two different high schools.

Verify at https://search.ccsd.net/schools/zoning/search/ by exact address. Skye Canyon's site says the community is near public and private schools but names none [source: https://skyecanyon.com/ | verified: 2026-07-25].

## Commute

Third-party estimates, which vary widely:

- To the Strip: reported as about 18 miles in one source and 22 to 25 miles in another, roughly 25 to 40 minutes via US 95 [source: https://www.thethomasgrouplv.com/skye-canyon-las-vegas/ | verified: 2026-07-25]
- To downtown Las Vegas: about 16 miles, roughly 25 to 35 minutes [source: https://www.thethomasgrouplv.com/skye-canyon-las-vegas/ | verified: 2026-07-25]
- To Harry Reid International Airport: NOT FOUND
- To the Henderson medical district: NOT FOUND

**Be honest in the guide:** the sources disagree with each other by seven miles. Skye Canyon is the farthest north of the six areas and the airport run is the longest of any area in this file. A buyer who flies for work should drive it themselves at 7 a.m. before they buy.

## The honest tradeoff

Skye Canyon gives you more house per dollar than Summerlin with a real, finished amenity core. The Skye Center, the fitness building with the junior Olympic pool, and the park exist today. You are also closer to Mount Charleston and the high desert than anywhere else in the valley, which matters if hiking and cooler summer weekends are part of why you are moving here. Entry pricing in the $400s is genuinely the lowest of any master plan on this list except Cadence and North Las Vegas.

The costs are distance and uncertainty. Skye Canyon is far north. Every trip to the airport, the Strip, or the south valley is a long one, and the published drive times do not agree with each other, which tells you they are soft. The SID exposure is the biggest unknown in this file, with internal estimates that varied enormously, so a buyer who skips the parcel lookup is genuinely gambling. And the master plan is roughly half built, so a chunk of what you are buying is still a promise. Providence, next door, is the opposite trade: finished, but the new inventory there is scattered infill rather than a growing community.

---

# AREA 3: HENDERSON, INSPIRADA AND CADENCE

Two very different master plans in the same city. Treat them separately.

---

## 3A. CADENCE

### Boundaries and character

Cadence sits in east Henderson, in ZIP 89011, inside the city's Eastside redevelopment area near the Sunset Industrial Corridor and Galleria at Sunset [source: https://www.cityofhenderson.com/government/departments/redevelopment/redevelopment-areas/eastside | verified: 2026-07-25].

The master plan describes itself as having "convenient access to Harry Reid International Airport, the Las Vegas Strip, downtown Las Vegas" and proximity to the Lake Mead National Recreation Area [source: https://www.cadencenv.com/ | verified: 2026-07-25].

Specific cross streets: NOT FOUND from the master plan's own materials.

### Who is building there now

Cadence's FAQ lists these homebuilders: **Beazer Homes, Century Communities, D.R. Horton, Lennar, Richmond American Homes, Taylor Morrison, and Woodside Homes** [source: https://cadencenv.com/faq/ | verified: 2026-07-25].

The main site's partner list adds rental and multifamily operators: Adler, American Homes 4 Rent, Ascend Symmetry, Avela Luxury Apartments, Element 12, and Elysian Homes [source: https://www.cadencenv.com/ | verified: 2026-07-25].

**This resolves an internal conflict.** Internal notes said Toll Brothers was an active Cadence builder. Toll Brothers does not appear on either Cadence list as of 2026-07-25, and Toll's own Las Vegas page lists no Cadence community [source: https://www.tollbrothers.com/luxury-homes-for-sale/Nevada/Las-Vegas | verified: 2026-07-25]. **Do not name Toll Brothers as a Cadence builder.** Beazer, which internal notes also questioned, is confirmed [source: https://cadencenv.com/faq/ | verified: 2026-07-25].

Product types range from paired townhomes to single family homes, plus apartments and build-to-rent product [source: https://www.cadencenv.com/ | verified: 2026-07-25].

### Price band

Cadence's own FAQ states: "Home prices vary from the $300,000s to the $700,000s" [source: https://cadencenv.com/faq/ | verified: 2026-07-25].

Richmond American communities listed on the Cadence new homes page [source: https://cadencenv.com/new-homes/ | verified: 2026-07-25]:

| Community | Product | Sq ft | Beds | From |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Duetto | Paired townhomes, two story | 1,300 to 1,520 | up to 3 | $234,950 |
| Capella | Single family, single story | 1,720 to 2,150 | up to 4 | $324,950 |
| Adagio | Single family, single story | 2,050 to 2,520 | up to 5 | $345,950 |

**Warning on this table:** the Cadence new homes page does not carry a publication date. The Duetto starting price of $234,950 sits well below the valleywide condo and townhome median of $292,000 for June 2026 [source: https://nevadabusiness.com/2026/07/lvr-reports-local-home-prices-hovering-at-record-high/ | verified: 2026-07-25]. That gap is large enough that the page may be stale. **Re-verify these three prices directly with Richmond American before printing them.**

### Master plan status

From Cadence's own FAQ [source: https://cadencenv.com/faq/ | verified: 2026-07-25]:

- **2,200 acres** of homes, parks, trails, and an urban core with retail and office space
- Up to **12,250 residential units** and 1.1 million square feet of commercial space at buildout
- Groundbreaking: **August 2013**. Sales began **December 2014**
- "Home sales and retail development will be released in multiple phases"

**This resolves an internal conflict.** Internal files carried three different Cadence totals (12,250 / 12,250 to 13,200 / 13,250). The master plan's own number is **up to 12,250 residential units** [source: https://cadencenv.com/faq/ | verified: 2026-07-25].

Amenities named by the developer [source: https://www.cadencenv.com/ | verified: 2026-07-25]:

- Central Park, approximately 50 acres
- Pools and splash pads
- Trails
- Schools

Additional features cited on the new homes page: Wi-Fi, bike share, dog park, pickleball courts [source: https://cadencenv.com/new-homes/ | verified: 2026-07-25].

**Which amenities are open versus planned: NOT FOUND.** The developer's materials do not distinguish. A buyer should ask, per amenity, in writing.

Buildout completion date: NOT FOUND from the developer.

### HOA reality

Cadence confirms the structure directly: "Yes, there is a master homeowners association as well as sub-associations" [source: https://cadencenv.com/faq/ | verified: 2026-07-25].

The Cadence new homes page states an HOA assessment of **$40 monthly** [source: https://cadencenv.com/new-homes/ | verified: 2026-07-25]. That figure appears alongside the Richmond American communities and is most likely the master assessment for those specific neighborhoods, not an all-in number, since the FAQ confirms sub-associations exist on top.

**All-in monthly HOA (master plus sub): NOT FOUND.** Get both figures from the builder in writing.

### SID and LID exposure

**This is Cadence's biggest selling point and it is confirmed by the developer.**

Cadence's FAQ states: "There are no SID/LID (special improvement district/limited improvement district) fees" [source: https://cadencenv.com/faq/ | verified: 2026-07-25].

The new homes page repeats it: "No SIDS/LIDS" [source: https://cadencenv.com/new-homes/ | verified: 2026-07-25].

**This resolves an internal conflict.** One internal report claimed "Cadence has its own LID structure; varies by parcel and neighborhood." The developer's own FAQ contradicts that. Two developer pages agree with each other.

**Still tell buyers to verify their own parcel** at https://amgnv.com/parcelsearch_non_pop1.asp. A developer FAQ is a marketing document. A parcel search is a record.

### Schools

Cadence expects to include three CCSD elementary schools, one CCSD middle school, and public charter schools at full buildout [source: https://www.reviewjournal.com/homes/advertising-features/cadence-in-henderson-adds-neighborhoods-retail-school-2547957/ | verified: 2026-07-25]. Note: this is a paid advertising feature in the Review-Journal, not news reporting. Label it as developer-supplied.

Cadence's FAQ mentions "neighborhood schools" without naming any [source: https://cadencenv.com/faq/ | verified: 2026-07-25].

Assigned schools by address: **NOT FOUND.** Verify at https://search.ccsd.net/schools/zoning/search/.

Henderson also has Fire Station 87, opened January 2023, serving Cadence [source: https://www.cityofhenderson.com/our-city/initiatives/education/schools | verified: 2026-07-25].

### Commute

Cadence claims convenient access to the airport, the Strip, and downtown Las Vegas [source: https://www.cadencenv.com/ | verified: 2026-07-25]. Specific mileage and drive times: **NOT FOUND** from any source I could verify.

Cadence is the closest of the six areas to Lake Mead and to the Henderson medical district, but I have no verified drive time. This is a gap the guide should either fill by measurement or state as unknown.

### The honest tradeoff

Cadence is the value play in Henderson, and the no-SID confirmation is real money. Over a 20 or 30 year bond term, a master plan with no special assessment can save a buyer thousands of dollars that a Skye Canyon or Inspirada buyer pays. The master HOA figure on the Richmond American communities is low. The 50-acre Central Park is a genuine amenity. Prices start in the $300,000s per the developer, which is the lowest floor of any Henderson master plan in this file. It is also relatively early in its life for a master plan of this size, so a buyer today gets a long runway of new retail and parks arriving around them.

The flip side is that east Henderson is not the Henderson most people picture. It is not Green Valley, it is not Anthem, and it is not near MacDonald Highlands. It sits next to the Sunset Industrial Corridor in the city's Eastside redevelopment area. The urban core, the retail, and most of the commercial square footage are still to come, which means today you are buying a residential neighborhood with a park, not a walkable town. The developer does not say which amenities are built and which are drawn. And a chunk of the partner list is apartments and single-family rental operators, so the neighborhood mix will include a meaningful share of renters. That is not a defect, but a buyer who assumed otherwise will be surprised.

---

## 3B. INSPIRADA

### Boundaries and character

Inspirada sits in the far southwest corner of Henderson in ZIP 89044, at the base of the Black Mountain foothills. Henderson Fire Station 91 opened in 2017 to serve it [source: https://www.cityofhenderson.com/our-city/initiatives/education/schools | verified: 2026-07-25].

Specific cross streets: NOT FOUND from a verified source.

### Who is building there now

The master developer is **Inspirada Builders LLC, a partnership of KB Home, Toll Brothers, and Tri Pointe Homes** [source: https://www.reviewjournal.com/business/housing/final-park-coming-to-popular-henderson-community-3177648/ | verified: 2026-07-25].

Confirmed active as of 2026-07-25:

- **Toll Brothers at Inspirada**, townhomes, from **$489,995** [source: https://www.tollbrothers.com/luxury-homes-for-sale/Nevada/Las-Vegas | verified: 2026-07-25]
- **KB Home** communities: the KB Home Las Vegas search returned no active communities on 2026-07-25, though the page image referenced "Gardens at Inspirada" [source: https://www.kbhome.com/new-homes-las-vegas | verified: 2026-07-25]. **KB Home's current Inspirada inventory: NOT FOUND.**

One third-party source reported that as of April 2026, only four quick move-in homes remained at Landings at Inspirada by KB Home [source: https://www.dulciecrawford.com/henderson-neighborhoods-approaching-final-inventory | verified: 2026-07-25]. Uncorroborated.

### Price band

Verified data point: Toll Brothers at Inspirada townhomes from **$489,995** as of 2026-07-25 [source: https://www.tollbrothers.com/luxury-homes-for-sale/Nevada/Las-Vegas | verified: 2026-07-25].

Full Inspirada price band: **NOT FOUND.** With inventory this thin, a range would be misleading anyway.

### Master plan status

**This is the most important thing about Inspirada and the guide should lead with it.**

Inspirada is at or near final buildout.

- Anticipated total homes at buildout: **7,500**. Population at the time of reporting: 18,000 residents [source: https://www.reviewjournal.com/business/housing/final-park-coming-to-popular-henderson-community-3177648/ | verified: 2026-07-25, article dated September 26, 2024]
- The community has **seven parks**. **Sentiero Park is the seventh and final one**, about 5 acres, at 2716 Via Napoli, built at a cost of $4.68 million, with a residents-only pool, basketball courts, picnic areas, playgrounds, and open grass. Expected completion was fall 2025 [source: https://www.reviewjournal.com/business/housing/final-park-coming-to-popular-henderson-community-3177648/ | verified: 2026-07-25]

**Note the conflict.** The Review-Journal reported 7,500 homes at buildout in September 2024. Internal files carried both "1,900+" and "about 13,500." Third-party sources say 1,940 acres and 8,500-plus homes. **Use the Review-Journal's 7,500 with its date attached, or write NOT FOUND. Do not use the internal numbers.**

**Whether Sentiero Park actually opened: NOT FOUND.** It was expected fall 2025. Confirm before the guide says the park system is complete.

**Practical consequence:** if Inspirada is genuinely down to a handful of quick move-in homes, it does not deserve a full section in a mid-2026 new construction guide. It deserves a short honest paragraph that says the master plan is finished, the amenities are all built, and buyers should look at resale here rather than new.

### HOA reality

Master and sub-association amounts: **NOT FOUND.** Inspirada's own site (inspirada.com) did not respond to automated retrieval on 2026-07-25 across three attempts. Third-party figures range from about $85 per month to considerably more and could not be corroborated.

### SID and LID exposure

**Inspirada carries LID assessments.** That is the consistent signal across every source, and it is the sharpest contrast with Cadence, which has none.

**Annual dollar amount: NOT FOUND.** Third-party estimates for the same community span from roughly $480 per year to roughly $3,600 per year. That is a 7x spread. I am not printing any of it.

The parcel lookup is the only reliable answer: https://amgnv.com/parcelsearch_non_pop1.asp, which covers City of Henderson districts [source: https://amgnv.com/parcelsearch_non_pop1.asp | verified: 2026-07-25]. Henderson bills its LIDs through AMG [source: https://www.cityofhenderson.com/government/departments/finance/lid-special-assessment-property-tax/lid-special-assessments | verified: 2026-07-25].

**Guide-worthy framing:** Cadence and Inspirada are two Henderson master plans about 20 miles apart, and one has no special assessment while the other does. Same city, same builder names, different carrying cost. That comparison is the single most useful thing a Henderson buyer can learn.

### Schools

Assigned CCSD schools: **NOT FOUND.** Verify at https://search.ccsd.net/schools/zoning/search/.

Unlike Summerlin West or Cadence, Inspirada's schools have existed for years, so assignment volatility is lower here. But still verify by address.

### Commute

**NOT FOUND** for the Strip, downtown, the airport, and the Henderson medical district. Inspirada is in the far south of the valley, so it is closer to the airport than Skye Canyon and farther from downtown than Cadence, but I have no verified figures.

### The honest tradeoff

Inspirada is the finished version of what Cadence is trying to become. Seven parks, all built. A walkable, dense street grid with paseos instead of six-foot block walls. Schools that already exist. A community that has had time to develop an actual identity, with 18,000 people living in it. If you want to know exactly what you are buying on day one, Inspirada removes almost all of the guesswork.

The problem is that there is almost nothing left to buy new. The master plan is at or near buildout, the final park was the seventh and last, and reported new inventory in 2026 is down to single digits at some communities. Whatever is left will be the lots and plans that nobody chose over the last several years. Inspirada also carries LID assessments, which Cadence does not, so your monthly carrying cost is higher for a comparable house. And it sits at the far southern edge of the valley, so if you work on the north or west side, the commute is real. For most buyers in 2026, the honest advice is that Inspirada is a resale market now, not a new construction market.

# AREA 4: UNION VILLAGE AND THE HENDERSON MEDICAL CORRIDOR

**Read this first: Union Village is a medical and commercial development, not a residential master plan.** Treating it as a place to buy a new house would mislead readers. The guide should scale this section accordingly.

## Boundaries and character

Union Village sits east of US 95 and Galleria Drive in Henderson [source: https://www.reviewjournal.com/life/health/desert-springs-hospital-medical-center-selects-new-ceo/attachment/construction-work-is-giving-shape-to-the-henderson-hospital-being-built-at-the-170-acre-union-village-development-east-of-u-s-95-and-galleria-drive-completion-of-henderson-hospital-is-expected-t/ | verified: 2026-07-25].

Reported size varies by source: 155 acres, 158 acres, and 170 acres all appear in Review-Journal coverage of different vintages [source: https://www.reviewjournal.com/news/henderson-sells-158-acres-for-union-village-health-center-project/ | verified: 2026-07-25]. **Exact acreage: NOT FOUND.** Use "roughly 155 to 170 acres" or omit.

The anchor is **Henderson Hospital**, which opened in November 2016 [source: https://www.lasvegasheals.org/henderson-hospital-opens-union-village/ | verified: 2026-07-25].

## What is actually built and what is still planned

**Built:**
- Henderson Hospital, opened November 2016 [source: https://www.lasvegasheals.org/henderson-hospital-opens-union-village/ | verified: 2026-07-25]
- A patient tower, $150 million, adding 93 beds with another 84 beds shelled for future growth, plus 30 additional emergency department beds and a three-story 480-space parking structure. Announced July 2020 with expected completion in late 2021 [source: https://www.hendersonhospital.com/about/news/construction-underway-new-patient-tower | verified: 2026-07-25]. **Note: this is 2020 news, not current construction. Any claim that a tower is "under construction now" is wrong.**
- An 85,000 square foot ambulatory surgery center and a medical office building [source: https://businesspress.vegas/real-estate/union-village-moves-forward-with-development-plans-19657/ | verified: 2026-07-25]
- Album Union Village, a gated 55-plus **rental** apartment community [source: https://www.55places.com/nevada/communities/album-union-village | verified: 2026-07-25]

**Planned, with no verified completion status:**
A 14,000 square foot dialysis clinic, a memory and dementia care village, a hotel, a 300-unit condominium buildout plus an additional condo project, a promenade, restaurants and retail, more apartments including senior living, and a 95,000 square foot Las Vegas Athletic Club [source: https://businesspress.vegas/real-estate/union-village-moves-forward-with-development-plans-19657/ | verified: 2026-07-25].

**Current 2025 or 2026 status of any of these: NOT FOUND.** The most recent substantive coverage I located is from 2019 through 2021.

**A caution the guide should carry:** Henderson and Union Village LLC had a legal dispute over the developer's failure to meet a park construction deadline, which the city council voted to settle [source: https://www.reviewjournal.com/local/henderson/henderson-settles-park-construction-dispute-with-major-developer-2334540/ | verified: 2026-07-25]. That is a documented, citable fact about schedule risk on this project. It does not accuse anyone of anything. It is a reason to be careful about promised amenities here.

## Who is building for-sale housing there

**One builder, one community, as of 2026-07-25.**

**The Townes at Union Village by Century Communities**, 1001 Gearus Place, Henderson, NV 89011 [source: https://www.centurycommunities.com/find-your-new-home/nevada/las-vegas-metro/henderson-nv/union-village/ | verified: 2026-07-25].

| Plan | Sq ft | Beds / baths | From |
|---|---|---|---|
| Residence 1405 | 1,405 | 3 bed, 2.5 bath | $335,990 |
| Residence 1478 | 1,478 | 3 bed, 2.5 bath | $339,990 |
| Residence 1479 | 1,479 | 3 bed, 2.5 bath | $352,990 |

Listed available homes ranged from **$349,000 to $371,000** [source: https://www.centurycommunities.com/find-your-new-home/nevada/las-vegas-metro/henderson-nv/union-village/ | verified: 2026-07-25].

**Data quality warning:** the quick move-in homes shown on that page listed move-in dates of August and September **2025**, which is ten to eleven months in the past. The page is very likely stale. **Call Century Communities and confirm whether this community is still selling before the guide names it.** Their online sales line is 702-936-3020 [source: https://www.centurycommunities.com/find-your-new-home/nevada/las-vegas-metro/ | verified: 2026-07-25].

Any second for-sale builder at Union Village: **NOT FOUND.** One builder does not make an area.

## Price band

**$335,990 to $371,000** for the only for-sale new construction identified [source: https://www.centurycommunities.com/find-your-new-home/nevada/las-vegas-metro/henderson-nv/union-village/ | verified: 2026-07-25]. Subject to the staleness warning above.

## HOA reality

**NOT FOUND.** The Century Communities community page does not list an HOA fee.

## SID and LID exposure

**NOT FOUND.** Union Village is in the City of Henderson, so any assessment would be a Henderson LID. Run the APN at https://amgnv.com/parcelsearch_non_pop1.asp.

## Schools

**NOT FOUND.** Verify at https://search.ccsd.net/schools/zoning/search/. Union Village is in ZIP 89011, the same ZIP as Cadence.

## Commute

The point of Union Village is that you do not commute to healthcare, healthcare is across the street. Drive times to the Strip, downtown, and the airport: **NOT FOUND.**

## The honest tradeoff

Union Village is a genuinely interesting idea, a health village where the hospital, the surgery center, the medical offices, and eventually senior housing and a dialysis clinic all sit on one campus. If you work at Henderson Hospital, or you are buying for a parent who will use it often, walking distance to a hospital is a real and rare thing in this valley. The one for-sale community is also the cheapest new construction in this entire file, in the $330,000s to low $370,000s for a three-bedroom townhome.

Everything else here is caution. There is one builder and one community, and its own web page appears to be showing move-in dates from last year, which suggests it may be closed out. Most of what makes Union Village sound appealing (the hotel, the promenade, the restaurants, the athletic club, the condos) is still on paper with no verified progress since roughly 2021, and the developer has a documented history of missing a construction deadline badly enough that the city sued and settled. You would be buying a townhome next to a hospital in a development whose second act has not clearly started. For most buyers, the honest recommendation is to look at Cadence, which is the same city, similar price floor, no SID or LID, and an actual residential community around it.

# AREA 5: SOUTHWEST LAS VEGAS (MOUNTAIN'S EDGE, ENTERPRISE, THE 215 CORRIDOR)

## Boundaries and character

**Enterprise** is the unincorporated Clark County township that covers most of the southwest valley. It runs roughly 66 square miles south of the 215 Beltway, starting near Fort Apache Road and Warm Springs Road and ending at I-15 and St. Rose Parkway [source: https://www.reviewjournal.com/business/what-is-the-history-of-enterprise-in-clark-county-3161832/ | verified: 2026-07-25].

Enterprise grew almost 60% from 2010 to 2023, compared with 20% for the valley overall, reaching **245,243 residents at the end of 2023** [source: https://www.reviewjournal.com/business/housing/this-town-in-the-southwest-valley-is-one-of-the-fastest-growing-areas-in-us-2931254/ | verified: 2026-07-25].

**Mountain's Edge** is a master plan inside the southwest, developed by Focus Property Group starting in 2004 [source: https://www.reviewjournal.com/business/what-is-the-history-of-enterprise-in-clark-county-3161832/ | verified: 2026-07-25]. Its master association office is at 8015 Blue Diamond Road, Suite 120, Las Vegas, NV 89178, phone 702-457-6362 [source: https://www.mymountainsedge.com/169/Amenities | verified: 2026-07-25].

Enterprise took off with the construction of the 215 Beltway and the development of the Rhodes Ranch, Mountain's Edge, and Southern Highlands master plans, all of which began more than 20 years ago [source: https://www.reviewjournal.com/business/what-is-the-history-of-enterprise-in-clark-county-3161832/ | verified: 2026-07-25].

Freeway access: the 215 Beltway across the north, I-15 to the east, St. Rose Parkway at the southeast corner.

## Who is building there now

**Full active builder list: NOT FOUND.** This is the weakest inventory coverage in the file, and there is a structural reason. Most southwest communities are filed under the bare city name "Las Vegas" with no township, village, or master plan label, so they cannot be reliably counted from any single source.

Confirmed presence:

- Century Communities lists Las Vegas metro inventory under ZIP codes **89113** (southwest Las Vegas) and **89178** (Mountain's Edge) [source: https://www.centurycommunities.com/find-your-new-home/nevada/las-vegas-metro/ | verified: 2026-07-25]
- Toll Brothers' Las Vegas list includes **Crestwood Ranch** (from $1,150,000), **Glenrock** (from $1,398,995), **Raven Crest** townhomes (from $634,995), **Elkhorn Grove** (from $644,995), and **The Loughton** condos (from $449,995), all filed as "Las Vegas, Clark County" with no master plan named [source: https://www.tollbrothers.com/luxury-homes-for-sale/Nevada/Las-Vegas | verified: 2026-07-25]. Which of these sit in the southwest: **NOT FOUND**

**Unresolved from internal research:** whether **Meritage Homes** is active in Clark County at all. One internal file said Meritage has no active Clark County communities and a closed local sales office. Another internal report named Meritage as a Mountain's Edge builder. I could not settle this externally on 2026-07-25. **Status: NOT FOUND. Do not name Meritage.**

## Price band

**Southern Highlands:** new homes from the $400,000s to over $1 million, with guard-gated golf course product above $1 million [source: https://www.nevadarealestategroup.com/enterprise/new-construction/ | verified: 2026-07-25]. Third-party, undated.

**Mountain's Edge and the broader southwest:** **NOT FOUND** from a source I could verify. Toll Brothers' Las Vegas communities without a named master plan span $449,995 (The Loughton condos) to $1,398,995 (Glenrock) [source: https://www.tollbrothers.com/luxury-homes-for-sale/Nevada/Las-Vegas | verified: 2026-07-25], which brackets the luxury end but says nothing about the middle.

**Recommendation:** the guide should give the southwest a wide, honest band and say plainly that this area has the widest price spread in the valley because it contains everything from starter product to guard-gated golf.

## Master plan status

**Mountain's Edge is essentially finished as a master plan.** Development began in 2004 [source: https://www.reviewjournal.com/business/what-is-the-history-of-enterprise-in-clark-county-3161832/ | verified: 2026-07-25].

Parks and amenities that exist today per the master association [source: https://www.mymountainsedge.com/169/Amenities | verified: 2026-07-25]:

- **Exploration Peak Park**, with a hike to the top of the peak and valley views
- **Paiute Park**
- **Nathaniel Jones Park**
- Multiple paseos and walking trails
- Rental spaces called the Legends Rooms

**Important distinction the association makes itself:** Mountain's Edge Regional Park is separately managed by Clark County and is **not** part of the master association [source: https://www.mymountainsedge.com/169/Amenities | verified: 2026-07-25]. Exploration Peak Park is at 9275 S Buffalo Drive, Las Vegas, NV 89178 and is in the Clark County parks system [source: https://parkslocator.clarkcountynv.gov/Search/ParkDetail?parkId=62 | verified: 2026-07-25].

**Total acreage, total homes, and buildout percentage: NOT FOUND** from the master association or from Focus Property Group. Third-party sources report roughly 3,500 acres and 12,000 to 12,500 homes, plus additional parks, a community center, and a magnet high school planned for 2027 or 2028 [source: https://www.nevadarealestategroup.com/blog/mountains-edge-southwest-las-vegas-master-plan-buyers-guide-2026/ | verified: 2026-07-25]. **Uncorroborated. Do not print as fact.**

**What this means for a buyer:** new construction in the southwest is mostly infill on leftover parcels, not a growing master plan. The parks and trails you see are the parks and trails you get. That is a plus for certainty and a minus for anyone expecting new amenities to arrive.

## HOA reality

**NOT FOUND.** The Mountain's Edge Master Association does not publish its assessment amount, billing frequency, or coverage on its public site. It provides only a payment portal link [source: https://www.mymountainsedge.com/ | verified: 2026-07-25].

Structure to expect: a master association covering the paseos, trails, and the three association parks, plus a sub-association in gated neighborhoods. Southern Highlands and Rhodes Ranch have their own separate structures. Get every number in writing.

Master association contact for an actual answer: 702-457-6362, Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. [source: https://www.mymountainsedge.com/169/Amenities | verified: 2026-07-25].

## SID and LID exposure

The southwest sits in **unincorporated Clark County**, so it falls under the Clark County districts listed in the shared section, not a city.

Confirmed on the Clark County collections schedule: **SID 121, Southern Highlands Area 2029**, due April 1 and October 1, final payment **October 1, 2029** [source: https://treasurer.co.clark.nv.us/Public_Web/Special_Assessments/Collections.aspx | verified: 2026-07-25].

**That is a genuinely useful buyer fact:** a Southern Highlands buyer can see a documented end date for that district. Fewer than four years of payments remain as of mid-2026.

No Mountain's Edge or Enterprise district appears by name on the current Clark County collections schedule [source: https://treasurer.co.clark.nv.us/Public_Web/Special_Assessments/Collections.aspx | verified: 2026-07-25]. That does not prove none exists on a given parcel. Older districts may have retired, and the schedule may not list every residential district. **Run the APN.**

## Schools

Assigned CCSD schools: **NOT FOUND.** Verify at https://search.ccsd.net/schools/zoning/search/.

A magnet high school focused on entrepreneurship is reported as planned for the Mountain's Edge area in 2027 or 2028 [source: https://www.nevadarealestategroup.com/blog/mountains-edge-southwest-las-vegas-master-plan-buyers-guide-2026/ | verified: 2026-07-25]. **Third-party and uncorroborated. Do not print without confirming with CCSD.**

## Commute

The 215 Beltway "provides connection to the Summerlin and Henderson communities and easy access to the airport and the Strip" [source: https://www.reviewjournal.com/business/what-is-the-history-of-enterprise-in-clark-county-3161832/ | verified: 2026-07-25].

Specific mileage and drive times to the Strip, downtown, the airport, and the Henderson medical district: **NOT FOUND.**

Structurally, the southwest is the closest of the six areas to Harry Reid International Airport, because the 215 runs directly to it along the south edge of the valley. But I have no verified drive time and will not invent one.

## The honest tradeoff

The southwest is the practical middle of the Las Vegas market. It has the best all-around freeway position of any area in this file, sitting on the 215 with quick shots to the airport, the Strip, and Henderson. It has the widest range of product in the valley, from condos in the $400,000s to guard-gated golf homes over $1 million, so almost any budget finds something. Enterprise is also the fastest-growing township in the region, which means retail, restaurants, and services keep arriving without you having to wait for a master developer to build them.

The honest weakness is that the southwest has no single identity and no single steward. Mountain's Edge is basically done, so its parks and trails will not grow. The master association will not tell you what your dues are without a phone call. New construction here is scattered infill rather than a coherent new village, so two houses a mile apart can sit in completely different HOA structures with completely different assessments, and there is no master plan website to explain it. This is the area where a buyer most needs someone to pull the parcel record, because there is no developer FAQ that will do it for them. It is also the least walkable of the six, built around arterial roads and block walls rather than paseos.

---

# AREA 6: NORTH LAS VEGAS

## Boundaries and character

North Las Vegas is its own incorporated city, not a neighborhood of Las Vegas. That matters, because its SIDs are city districts and its permits, police, and fire are city services.

The newest construction clusters in the far north, in the **Villages at Tule Springs** and **Valley Vista**, both near the 215 Beltway [source: https://visitvegashomes.com/villages-at-tule-springs | verified: 2026-07-25] [source: https://www.valleyvistanlv.org/about-us/ | verified: 2026-07-25].

**Villages at Tule Springs** is near the 215 Beltway close to Aliante, with access to the two Air Force bases [source: https://visitvegashomes.com/villages-at-tule-springs | verified: 2026-07-25]. A newer phase called Village 2 is planned on six parcels off North 5th Street and the 215 Beltway [source: https://www.reviewjournal.com/business/housing/hundreds-of-more-homes-approved-for-north-las-vegas-3349895/ | verified: 2026-07-25].

**Valley Vista** is in North Las Vegas near Nellis Air Force Base [source: https://www.valleyvistanlv.org/about-us/ | verified: 2026-07-25].

## Who is building there now

**Villages at Tule Springs:** three builders across seven neighborhoods, reported as **Tri Pointe Homes, KB Home, and Lennar** [source: https://visitvegashomes.com/villages-at-tule-springs | verified: 2026-07-25]. Third-party source, no stated date.

Tri Pointe homes at Villages at Tule Springs are reported at 1,954 to 3,892 square feet with 3 to 6 bedrooms [source: https://visitvegashomes.com/villages-at-tule-springs | verified: 2026-07-25].

KB Home received approval for 700 additional homes in North Las Vegas [source: https://www.reviewjournal.com/business/housing/hundreds-of-more-homes-approved-for-north-las-vegas-3349895/ | verified: 2026-07-25].

**Valley Vista:** D.R. Horton and Lennar built there between 2018 and 2024, with D.R. Horton plans from 1,200 to over 4,400 square feet in single family and townhome product [source: https://visitvegashomes.com/valley-vista | verified: 2026-07-25]. Third-party.

Century Communities lists Las Vegas metro inventory under ZIP **89031**, which is North Las Vegas [source: https://www.centurycommunities.com/find-your-new-home/nevada/las-vegas-metro/ | verified: 2026-07-25].

**Full current builder roster: NOT FOUND** from a primary source. Neither master plan publishes a live builder list I could retrieve.

## Price band

**North Las Vegas median home price: $415,000**, up 0.02% year over year [source: https://www.houzeo.com/housing-market/nevada/north-las-vegas | verified: 2026-07-25]. This is an all-homes figure from a third-party aggregator, not new construction and not MLS.

New construction listings in North Las Vegas showed a median listing price of about **$425,000** with examples ranging roughly **$408,900 to $486,900** [source: https://redfin.com/city/13363/NV/North-Las-Vegas/amenity/new+construction | verified: 2026-07-25]. Small sample, third-party, treat as directional.

**The useful comparison:** North Las Vegas is the only one of the six areas where the typical new home sits below the valleywide existing single-family median of $490,000 for June 2026 [source: https://nevadabusiness.com/2026/07/lvr-reports-local-home-prices-hovering-at-record-high/ | verified: 2026-07-25].

## Master plan status

**Villages at Tule Springs:** reported at **1,280 acres with 8,683 homes planned at final buildout**, with a first phase of 1,000 homes, a 35-acre regional park, and a City of North Las Vegas police station [source: https://visitvegashomes.com/villages-at-tule-springs | verified: 2026-07-25]. Third-party. **Not corroborated by a developer or city source.** Whether the 35-acre park and the police station are open or still planned: **NOT FOUND.**

**Valley Vista**, per its own community association [source: https://www.valleyvistanlv.org/about-us/ | verified: 2026-07-25]:

- Construction began **2017**
- Master plan completion: **January 2026**
- Total planned homes: **3,469**
- Built and open: **Galaxy Park, 9 acres**, plus an emergency room facility, a detention basin, and multifamily communities
- Still planned: an **elementary school** and an **Albertsons** grocery store

**Read that carefully.** Valley Vista's own association says the master plan reached completion in January 2026 while the elementary school and the grocery store are still listed as planned. A buyer moving in today should not assume either exists. That is exactly the kind of gap the guide exists to catch.

## HOA reality

**Valley Vista:** the association is the Valley Vista Community Association, Inc. Assessment amount and coverage: **NOT FOUND** [source: https://www.valleyvistanlv.org/about-us/ | verified: 2026-07-25].

**Villages at Tule Springs:** **NOT FOUND.**

Get both master and sub-association figures in writing from the builder.

## SID and LID exposure

North Las Vegas is its own city and forms its own improvement districts. The AMG parcel search explicitly covers **City of North Las Vegas** districts [source: https://amgnv.com/parcelsearch_non_pop1.asp | verified: 2026-07-25].

No North Las Vegas district appears on the Clark County collections schedule, which is expected, because those are county districts [source: https://treasurer.co.clark.nv.us/Public_Web/Special_Assessments/Collections.aspx | verified: 2026-07-25].

**Annual dollar amount: NOT FOUND.** Run the APN.

**Worth flagging in the guide:** far-north master plans built on raw desert typically require the most new infrastructure, which is what SIDs finance. A buyer who is drawn to North Las Vegas specifically because the sticker price is lower should check the assessment before assuming the total monthly cost is lower too. That framing is honest and does not require a number.

## Schools

Assigned CCSD schools: **NOT FOUND.** Verify at https://search.ccsd.net/schools/zoning/search/.

**Special caution for Valley Vista:** the community association lists an elementary school as planned, not open [source: https://www.valleyvistanlv.org/about-us/ | verified: 2026-07-25]. A family buying here should confirm with CCSD which existing school their address is currently zoned to, and how far away it is, rather than counting on the planned one.

## Commute

**NOT FOUND** for the Strip, downtown, the airport, and the Henderson medical district.

Structural note that does not require a number: the far-north master plans sit at the top of the valley on the 215, which puts them close to Nellis Air Force Base and to Creech Air Force Base access, and far from the airport and Henderson. The two Air Force bases are cited as an access advantage for Villages at Tule Springs [source: https://visitvegashomes.com/villages-at-tule-springs | verified: 2026-07-25].

## The honest tradeoff

North Las Vegas is where a first-time buyer can still get a new house with a yard for less than the valley's median resale price. The far-north master plans are new, so the homes are current-code and energy efficient, and lot sizes tend to be more generous than what the same money buys in Summerlin or Henderson. If you are stationed at Nellis or you work on the north side, the location is genuinely convenient rather than a compromise.

The tradeoffs are amenity risk and distance. Valley Vista's own association says the master plan finished in January 2026 while the elementary school and the grocery store are still on the planned list, which is a hard lesson in the difference between a finished street grid and a finished community. Tule Springs is even earlier, and I could not verify from any developer or city source whether the promised 35-acre park and police station are open. You are also at the top of the valley, so the airport and Henderson are long drives, and there is less established retail and dining nearby than in any other area in this file. North Las Vegas also carries a separate reputational question in the resale market that a buyer should understand going in, though the numbers show prices holding roughly flat year over year rather than falling [source: https://www.houzeo.com/housing-market/nevada/north-las-vegas | verified: 2026-07-25].

# WHICH AREA FITS WHICH BUYER

The guide has three reader paths. This matrix maps the six areas to them. It is a judgment framework built on the verified facts above, not a fact table.

## Path 1: Relocating from out of state

You do not know the valley yet. Your biggest risk is buying into a promise that never gets built, or into a commute you did not understand.

| Area | Fit | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **Summerlin** | **Strongest fit** | The amenities exist today, not on a rendering. Deep resale market if the move does not stick. Least guesswork of any area. Cost: no new construction under roughly $500,000. |
| **Inspirada** | Strong fit, but for resale | Seven parks all built, established schools, 18,000 residents. But it is at or near buildout, so there is almost nothing new to buy. |
| **Skye Canyon** | Good fit with homework | Real, finished amenity core (Skye Center, Skye Fitness, the park) at a lower entry price than Summerlin. The catch is distance and unverified SID exposure. |
| **Cadence** | Conditional | Best carrying cost story in the file (no SID or LID, low master HOA). But the urban core is not built and east Henderson is not the Henderson most out-of-state buyers picture. Go see it in person first. |
| **Southwest / Mountain's Edge** | Conditional | Best freeway position and widest price range. But no single master plan identity and no developer FAQ to explain what you are buying. Needs a local to pull records. |
| **North Las Vegas** | Weakest fit | Lowest entry price, but the highest gap between what is drawn and what is open, and the least established surrounding retail. Hard to evaluate from out of state. |
| **Union Village** | Not recommended as a first move | One builder, one community, a possibly stale sales page, and a mostly unbuilt second phase. |

## Path 2: Moving up locally

You already know the valley. You are trading a first home for a bigger one and you care about carrying cost and resale.

| Area | Fit | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **Summerlin** | **Strongest fit** | The move-up product is here. Kestrel, Grand Park, and Stonebridge run from the $500Ks to $2M-plus, so you can size the jump. Best resale depth. |
| **Cadence** | **Strongest fit on cost** | The developer states there are no SID or LID fees. Over a 20 or 30 year bond term that is real money against a comparable Inspirada or Skye Canyon house. |
| **Southwest / Mountain's Edge** | Strong fit | Widest product ladder in the valley, from $450K condos to $1.4M single family, all with the same 215 access. Easy to move up without changing your commute. |
| **Skye Canyon** | Good fit | Toll Brothers from $665,000 is a genuine move-up option with a finished amenity core. Verify the SID before you compare monthly payments. |
| **Inspirada** | Limited | Almost no new inventory. Look here on resale. |
| **North Las Vegas** | Limited | Product ceiling is lower. Better as a first purchase than a move-up. |
| **Union Village** | No | Townhome product only, and its status is unclear. |

## Path 3: First new build

This is your first newly built home. You are most exposed to the surprises: the SID, the second HOA, the lot premium, the amenity that never arrives.

| Area | Fit | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **Cadence** | **Strongest fit** | Prices from the $300,000s per the developer, a stated master HOA of $40 monthly on some communities, and a documented no-SID-or-LID position. The fewest hidden-cost surprises of any area in this file. |
| **North Las Vegas** | **Strong fit on price** | The only area where typical new construction sits below the valleywide $490,000 existing-home median. Just verify the SID and confirm which school is actually open. |
| **Skye Canyon** | Good fit, with one condition | From the $400s with real amenities. Do not sign until you have run the parcel through AMG. This is the area where the SID surprise is most likely. |
| **Southwest / Mountain's Edge** | Conditional | Plenty of options, but the least transparent HOA and district structure. You need someone pulling records for you. |
| **Summerlin** | Stretch | No entry-level product. If you can reach the mid $500Ks, you get the most certainty in the valley. |
| **Union Village** | Only if verified | Cheapest new construction found in this file at $335,990, and walking distance to a hospital. But confirm the community is still selling before you get attached. |
| **Inspirada** | No | Nothing meaningful left to build. |

## The one question every reader should ask, in every area

**"What is the annual special assessment on this exact lot, what is the remaining balance, what year does it end, and what is the prepayment penalty?"**

Ask it in writing. Get the APN. Run it at https://amgnv.com/parcelsearch_non_pop1.asp. This is the single biggest surprise cost in Las Vegas new construction, the amount varies enormously even inside one master plan, and no builder brochure in this file publishes it.

---

# GAPS AND OPEN ITEMS FOR THE ORCHESTRATOR

Ranked by how much they would improve the guide.

1. **Per-community SID and LID annual dollar amounts.** NOT FOUND everywhere. No government or developer source publishes them. The only fix is running actual APNs through AMG or calling AMG at 702-796-0082. If someone can run five to eight representative parcels, that single table would be the most valuable page in the guide.
2. **HOA monthly amounts, master and sub.** NOT FOUND for Summerlin, Skye Canyon, Mountain's Edge, Inspirada, Valley Vista, and Tule Springs. Only Cadence publishes a number, and only for some communities. Every master association hides this behind a phone call.
3. **Drive times.** NOT FOUND for most area-to-destination pairs. The few numbers available come from travel blogs and disagree with each other by up to seven miles for the same route. Consider measuring these directly rather than citing.
4. **Whether The Townes at Union Village is still selling.** Its own page shows 2025 move-in dates. Call 702-936-3020 before the guide names it.
5. **Whether Sentiero Park at Inspirada opened.** Expected fall 2025, unconfirmed.
6. **Whether Valley Vista's elementary school and Albertsons opened.** The association still lists both as planned after stating the master plan completed in January 2026.
7. **Whether Pulte and Lennar are still active at Skye Canyon.** Internal reports say yes, the master plan site does not list them.
8. **Whether Meritage Homes is active in Clark County.** Internal sources flatly contradict each other and I could not settle it externally.
9. **City of Las Vegas SID district numbers and boundaries.** The city does not publish a public district list comparable to Clark County's collections schedule. SID 610 for Skye Canyon Phase 3 comes from a third-party source only.
10. **Mountain's Edge total acreage, total homes, and buildout status** from Focus Property Group or the master association. Only third-party figures exist.
11. **Providence total homes and acreage.** Two third-party sources give wildly different numbers (5,600 on 1,200 acres versus 8,500 on 4,200 acres).
12. **Summerlin percent built out.** Third parties say over 80%. No Howard Hughes source confirms it.
13. **Cadence's Richmond American prices.** The Duetto from $234,950 sits far below the valleywide townhome median and the page is undated. Re-verify with the builder.
